rec-20261116-5286.point: LS Power Grid proposes a company-specific way to recover the cost of upgrades driven by large loads.
rec-20261116-5286.quote: a transparent, company-specific mechanism for LS Power Grid to recover the costs of transmission upgrades that are identified as necessary

rec-20261116-5286.point: No upgrade is listed yet, so the filing does not change current rates.
rec-20261116-5286.quote: No Large Load-Driven Upgrade is listed in proposed Table 1 as of the requested effective date

rec-20261116-5286.point: An upgrade enters the rate only after a separate section 205 filing adds it to the table.
rec-20261116-5286.quote: a Large Load-Driven Upgrade becomes an Eligible Project only after Commission acceptance of a section 205 filing adding it to Table 1

rec-20261116-5286.point: The agreement sets a fixed annual minimum revenue contribution for each covered upgrade.
rec-20261116-5286.quote: the CRA establishes a fixed Annual Minimum Transmission Revenue Contribution (“Annual MTRC”)

rec-20261116-5286.point: The contribution runs 20 years from the upgrade's in-service date.
rec-20261116-5286.quote: MTRC Term begins on the actual Upgrade In-Service Date and ends on the day immediately preceding its twentieth anniversary

rec-20261116-5286.point: Operational security equals all remaining revenue responsibility.
rec-20261116-5286.quote: The CRA requires Operational Security equal to one hundred percent (100%) of the nominal Remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility

rec-20261116-5286.point: Retail security can offset it dollar for dollar if the customer certifies it is available and enforceable.
rec-20261116-5286.quote: the direct Operational Security requirement may be reduced dollar-for-dollar by qualifying retail security support only where the Eligible Customer delivers a current Retail Security Certification

rec-20261116-5286.point: It calls the termination fee an accelerated contractual charge, not a penalty.
rec-20261116-5286.quote: The Termination Fee is an accelerated contractual termination charge, not a penalty

filing-er27-517-nyiso-large-loads.point: NYISO says the revisions fully answer FERC's concerns within its own filing rights.
filing-er27-517-nyiso-large-loads.quote: They are intended to fully satisfy the concerns raised by the Commission

filing-er27-517-nyiso-large-loads.point: It proposes Firm and Non-Firm Withdrawal Service rather than the three services FERC created for PJM.
NYISO explains why it will not adopt the three PJM co-location services.
filing-er27-517-nyiso-large-loads.quote: Part V explains why the NYISO is not proposing to adopt the three new transmission services that the Commission established in the PJM Co-Location Order

filing-er27-517-nyiso-large-loads.point: Non-firm service would be curtailed when the local price reaches $200 per megawatt-hour.
filing-er27-517-nyiso-large-loads.quote: establish a rule under which Non-Firm Withdrawal Service would be curtailed when the applicable nodal Locational- Based Marginal Price (“LBMP”) for a Large Load reaches $200 MW/h

filing-er27-517-nyiso-large-loads.point: The New York transmission owners file a separate two-party cost recovery agreement.
filing-er27-517-nyiso-large-loads.quote: the NYTOs will submit a new two-party pro forma cost recovery agreement to address the cost- shifting issues discussed in the Show Cause Order

filing-er27-517-nyiso-large-loads.point: NYISO's study cycle would take about 18 to 24 months, with a 90-day system impact study inside it.
filing-er27-517-nyiso-large-loads.quote: between one year and six months and two years, including a 90-day period for the performance of the System Impact Study

filing-er27-517-nyiso-large-loads.point: The new study process includes a description of how alternative transmission technologies will be considered.
filing-er27-517-nyiso-large-loads.quote: (x) describe how alternative transmission technologies will be considered

filing-er27-517-nyiso-large-loads.point: NYISO ties paired generation to the same capacity region as the load instead of using the order's electrically proximate test.
filing-er27-517-nyiso-large-loads.quote: use Associated Resource rules tied to NYISO Capacity Regions in lieu of the Show Cause Order’s “electrically proximate resource

filing-er27-517-nyiso-large-loads.point: A partner resource serving a large load must be in the same capacity region as that load.
filing-er27-517-nyiso-large-loads.quote: for a Partner Resource Arrangement, the Resource must be located in the same Capacity Region as the given Large Load.

filing-er27-517-nyiso-large-loads.point: NYISO adds a co-located load and generator arrangement that lets the load take firm withdrawal service.
filing-er27-517-nyiso-large-loads.quote: Large Loads or portions thereof and an “Associated Resource(s)” that enter into a “Co-Located Arrangement” or “Partner Resource Arrangement” so that the Large Load may be served via some amount of Firm Withdrawal Service

rec-20261116-5335.point: NYISO's filing sets the study process and services. The owners' filing covers cost recovery and operations.
rec-20261116-5335.quote: While the NYISO’s filing establishes the study process, readiness requirements, and new Firm and Non-Firm Withdrawal Services for Large Loads, the NYTOs’ filing addresses the complementary elements necessary to recover the costs of facilities built to serve Large Loads

rec-20261116-5335.point: Each owner recovers all allocated upgrade and facility costs from the large load customer.
rec-20261116-5335.quote: recover 100% of the costs of Network Upgrades and Attachment Facilities allocated to a Large Load Customer

rec-20261116-5335.point: Recovery runs over 15 years, without accelerated depreciation.
rec-20261116-5335.quote: that compresses cost recovery into a 15-year term without accelerated depreciation

rec-20261116-5335.point: The customer posts security that the owner can draw on if the project is abandoned or the customer defaults.
rec-20261116-5335.quote: requires the Large Load Customer to post security for those allocated costs, which the Transmission Owner may draw upon in the event of abandonment of a Large Load project, default, or other specified events

rec-20261116-5335.point: Non-firm withdrawal service would be limited to thermal and resource adequacy constraints.
rec-20261116-5335.quote: limit Non-Firm Withdrawal Service to thermal and resource adequacy constraints

rec-20261116-5335.point: The owners propose no new delivery rates. Section 5 keeps pointing to state-approved rates.
rec-20261116-5335.quote: Section 5 will continue to reference the voltage-differentiated delivery rates and service classifications approved by the New York Public Service Commission

rec-20261116-5335.point: The owners will contract with the large load customer directly, not with energy service companies or other intermediaries.
rec-20261116-5335.quote: They do not volunteer to enter into Facilities Study, Security, Cost Recovery, and Interconnection Agreements with ESCOs or other intermediaries of Large Load Customers

rec-20261116-5335.point: Most revisions would take effect February 1, 2027, matching NYISO's filing.
rec-20261116-5335.quote: request an effective date for the revisions to Attachment LL and Attachment B of Section 8 of the NYISO OATT of February 1, 2027

rec-20261116-5335.point: The owners' agreement for facilities studies sets fixed deposits and a schedule inside NYISO's study timeline.
rec-20261116-5335.quote: a pro forma Facilities Study Agreement provides a uniform framework, fixed study deposits, and a defined schedule for the Facilities Studies the Transmission Owners perform under Attachment LL

rec-20261116-5335.point: The owners add operating requirements for large loads paired with co-located or partner generation.
rec-20261116-5335.quote: operating requirements that apply to Large Loads interconnected under the LLIP, including Large Loads that take Non-Firm Transmission Withdrawal Service at a level below their maximum potential withdrawal and Large Loads paired with Co-Located or Partner Resources
